s1.title: Managing your team
s1.description: Every member’s access comes down to three things: which Portal they log into, their Role, and the Region they work in. This quick tour shows where each lives.

s2.title: Members vs Invitations
s2.description: “Members” are people already in your organization. “Invitations” are pending email invites that haven’t been accepted yet.

s3.title: Seats
s3.description: Your plan includes a number of Admin (Tenant portal) and User (User portal) seats. Each member uses one — these badges show how many are left.

s4.title: Invite someone
s4.description: Inviting asks for Portal → Role → Region. Pick the portal for the kind of work they’ll do, a role that matches their job, and the region whose data they need.

s5.title: That’s it
s5.description: You can change a member’s role, status, or regions anytime from the Edit action. Open Help → “How access works” for the full picture.

s1.title: Creating a contract
s1.description: Fill in the contract’s identity, then its value & term, then ownership. The uploaded file becomes the contract’s first document (OCR-indexed for search).

s2.title: Contract type
s2.description: The type drives defaults like risk tier and whether legal review is required. Manage the catalog under Contracts → Types.

s3.title: Department & folder
s3.description: Department tags the contract to your org structure (reporting + approval routing). Folder just organizes it in the explorer — neither changes who can see it.

s4.title: Counterparty & IDD
s4.description: Link the third party so its due-diligence status is visible. If you require IDD clearance, the contract can’t be executed until that party is cleared.

s1.title: Your case library
s1.description: This is a file-explorer for litigation cases. Use folders to group them however you like — folders never change who can access a case or its region.

s2.title: Folders & Home
s2.description: Home shows unfiled cases; click a folder to see its cases. A case lives in exactly one folder, or none.

s3.title: New folder
s3.description: Create folders to organize cases by matter, client, year — whatever suits you.

s4.title: New case
s4.description: Start a case here. If you’re inside a folder, the new case lands in it automatically.

s1.title: Departments
s1.description: Departments mirror your internal structure (Department › Sub-Department / Cost Center › Function). They tag contracts and cases for reporting and approval routing — they don’t control who can see data.

s2.title: Add a department
s2.description: Create a top-level department, then nest sub-departments under it. Assign a Head of Department and a cost center if you track them.

welcome.title: 👋 Quick form guide
welcome.text: This tour walks you through each section of the report form. It takes about 60 seconds. Your identity is protected throughout — you control whether to stay anonymous.

category.title: 📋 Incident category
category.text: Start by picking the category that best describes what you witnessed — for example, fraud, harassment, or safety violation. If unsure, choose the closest match.

description.title: ✍️ What happened?
description.text: Describe the incident in as much detail as you can — who was involved, what occurred, where, when, and how you know about it. The more detail you provide, the easier it is to investigate. Do not include your own name if you want to stay anonymous.

location.title: 📍 Location
location.text: Fill in as much location detail as you know — the specific site, city, or region where the incident occurred. This helps route your report to the right team. All fields here are optional.

relationship.title: 🔗 Your relationship
relationship.text: Let us know how you relate to the organization — employee, contractor, supplier, etc. This helps us understand the context of your report. This field is optional.

involved.title: 👤 Involved persons
involved.text: Add the name(s) of anyone directly engaged in the behavior you’re reporting. First name, last name, and job title are all optional — provide whatever you know.

dates.title: 📅 Timing
dates.text: Tell us when the incident happened and whether it’s ongoing. Even approximate dates (like “last month”) help investigators establish a timeline.

anonymous.title: 🔒 Stay anonymous?
anonymous.text: By default your report is anonymous — we never know who you are. If you’d like to receive updates on your case, uncheck this box and provide a contact email. Your details are kept strictly confidential.

conflict.title: 🛡️ Conflict of interest
conflict.text: If your report involves a member of the compliance team, tick their name here to hide this case from them. Your report will still reach the Compliance Administrator.

submit.title: ✅ Ready to submit
submit.text: Accept the terms and click Submit report. You’ll immediately receive a case reference number — save it to track your report’s progress without revealing your identity.
